questions.question: To whom was Gond king Dalpat married?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Durgawati**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Dalpat Shah**, a Gond king of the Garha Mandla kingdom, was married to **Rani Durgawati**, a princess of the Chandel dynasty.
 
• **Rani Durgawati** was renowned for her beauty, valor, and administrative acumen, becoming a symbol of bravery and resistance in Indian history.
 
• After the death of Dalpat Shah in **1548**, Rani Durgawati ruled the kingdom as regent for her son, **Veer Narayan**, demonstrating exceptional governance and military capabilities.
 
• She fought valiantly against the Mughal forces led by **Asaf Khan** in **1564**, but ultimately sacrificed her life in battle rather than surrendering to the invaders.
 
• Her reign is remembered for her efforts to protect the independence of her kingdom and her legacy continues to inspire many as an iconic historical figure.

questions.question: Which of the following is a Fundamental Duty mentioned in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: To value the rich heritage of our composite ​culture
To not indulge in corrupt practices
To respect freedom of speech of others

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To value the rich heritage of our composite culture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Duties** were introduced in the Indian Constitution through the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**, based on the recommendations of the **Swaran Singh Committee**. They are enshrined in **Article 51A**.
 
• One of the Fundamental Duties includes the obligation to **value and preserve the rich heritage of India’s composite culture**. This duty aims to inspire citizens to protect and promote India's diverse cultural legacy.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are applicable to **all Indian citizens**, and while they are not enforceable by law, they serve as a moral obligation to uphold the spirit of the Constitution.
 
• The statement “To value the rich heritage of our composite culture” is directly mentioned in **Article 51A(f)**, making it a part of the Fundamental Duties.
 
• Other duties include respecting the Constitution, promoting harmony, safeguarding public property, and striving for excellence, all of which aim to foster a sense of responsibility among citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Duties Overview:**

 
 
• There are currently **11 Fundamental Duties** listed under **Article 51A** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These duties were inspired by the **Constitution of the USSR** and aim to promote patriotism and strengthen the unity of the nation.
 
• While these duties are non-justiciable, they complement Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles of State Policy.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976:**
 
 
• The **42nd Amendment** is also known as the “Mini Constitution” due to the extensive changes it brought to the Indian Constitution.
 
• Besides introducing Fundamental Duties, it emphasized the importance of Directive Principles and strengthened the powers of the central government.
 
 
 
• **Preservation of Composite Culture:**
 
 
• India is known for its **diverse culture and heritage**, including monuments, art forms, languages, festivals, and traditions.
 
• The duty to preserve this heritage encourages citizens to actively participate in cultural preservation initiatives such as protecting historical sites and promoting cultural awareness.
 
• Examples include the **Clean India Campaign** to preserve heritage sites and cultural festivals such as **Surajkund Mela** and **International Yoga Day**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• While **Fundamental Rights** are enforceable by the judiciary and provide protection to individuals, **Fundamental Duties** serve as moral obligations for citizens.
 
• Both aim to uphold the democratic framework of India and ensure the holistic development of society.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **List of Fundamental Duties:** **Article 51A** lists duties such as respecting the Constitution, cherishing national heritage, promoting harmony, and safeguarding public property.
 
• **Enforcement:** While Fundamental Duties are not legally enforceable, several initiatives like cultural education programs and civic awareness campaigns promote adherence.
 
• **Global Context:** Countries like **Japan** and **Russia** also emphasize citizen duties in their constitutions, highlighting the universal importance of moral obligations.
 
• **Civic Awareness:** Schools and colleges in India conduct programs to instill the importance of Fundamental Duties among students.

questions.question: Which of the following writ is issued by a higher court (High Court or Supreme Court) when a lower court has considered a case going beyond its jurisdiction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prohibition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prohibition** is a writ issued by a higher court, such as the **High Court or Supreme Court**, to prevent a lower court or tribunal from exceeding its jurisdiction in hearing a case.
 
• This writ acts as a tool to ensure that judicial proceedings remain within the boundaries of the **legal authority** granted to the concerned judicial body.
 
• The writ of Prohibition is issued when a lower court or tribunal attempts to act beyond its jurisdiction or violates procedural laws.
 
• Prohibition is issued only to prevent an act from being done; it does not correct any action that has already been completed.
 
• It is a preventive measure and differs from other writs such as **Certiorari**, which is corrective in nature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Writs in the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• The Indian Constitution provides for five types of writs under **Article 32** (Supreme Court) and **Article 226** (High Courts).
 
• These writs are **Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari,** and **Quo Warranto**.
 
• These writs serve as tools to enforce fundamental rights and ensure judicial accountability.
 
 
 
• **Explanation of Other Writs:**
 
 
• **Habeas Corpus:** A writ issued to ensure the release of a person unlawfully detained. It protects the **personal liberty** of individuals.
 
• **Mandamus:** A writ directing a public authority to perform a duty it is legally obligated to fulfill.
 
• **Certiorari:** A writ issued to transfer a case from a lower court to a higher court or to quash an order passed by a lower court that exceeds its jurisdiction.
 
• **Quo Warranto:** A writ questioning the legality of a person's claim to a public office.
 
 
 
• **Key Characteristics of Prohibition:**
 
 
• **Jurisdictional Aspect:** Prohibition ensures that lower courts function within their legal jurisdiction.
 
• **Preventive Nature:** It prevents unlawful actions before they occur, unlike Certiorari, which corrects actions that have already happened.
 
• **Recipient:** It can only be issued to judicial and quasi-judicial bodies, not administrative authorities.
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• Suppose a lower court decides to hear a matter related to international treaties, which is beyond its jurisdiction. The higher court can issue a writ of Prohibition to stop the proceedings.
 
• If a tribunal begins proceedings in violation of procedural rules laid down by statute, Prohibition can be issued to halt such proceedings.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 32 and Article 226:**

 
 
• While **Article 32** empowers the Supreme Court to issue writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights, **Article 226** gives similar powers to High Courts for both fundamental rights and other legal rights.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Review:** Prohibition is an integral part of the judicial review mechanism that ensures legal compliance and prevents abuse of power by lower courts and tribunals.
 
• **Limitations:** The writ cannot be issued against legislative bodies, private individuals, or administrative authorities acting in non-judicial capacities.

questions.question: In the context of BBIN motor vehicle agreement, what does "I" stands for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **BBIN Motor Vehicle Agreement:** BBIN stands for **Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, and Nepal**. It is a regional agreement aimed at improving motor vehicle transportation and connectivity between these four countries.
 
• The letter "I" in BBIN represents **India**, which is one of the key participants in the agreement.
 
• The agreement was signed on **15th June 2015** in **Thimphu, Bhutan**, to facilitate seamless movement of passenger, personal, and cargo vehicles across borders.
 
• **Objective:** The BBIN agreement promotes economic integration and trade facilitation by enabling easier and faster movement of goods and people across borders in South Asia.
 
• India has been an active proponent of the agreement, recognizing the importance of regional connectivity for boosting trade and cooperation among neighboring countries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Significance of BBIN Agreement:**

 
 
• The BBIN Motor Vehicle Agreement is a milestone in regional cooperation in South Asia, ensuring smoother transportation and logistics across borders.
 
• It facilitates trade by reducing transportation time and costs, enabling economic growth in the region.
 
• The agreement enhances connectivity and cooperation in areas such as tourism, trade, and cultural exchange.
 
 
 
• **Implementation:**
 
 
• The agreement allows the transit of goods and passenger vehicles with simplified procedures such as mutual recognition of permits and vehicle registration documents.
 
• Each participating country is responsible for implementing the agreement and ensuring that infrastructure and regulatory frameworks align with its objectives.
 
 
 
• **Challenges:**
 
 
• The agreement faces challenges due to political and administrative differences among the member countries.
 
• Bhutan has expressed reservations about the agreement, citing environmental concerns and other issues.
 
 
 
• **India’s Role:**
 
 
• India plays a pivotal role in the BBIN agreement, emphasizing the importance of connectivity for regional development.
 
• India has invested in infrastructure development to facilitate the implementation of the agreement, such as improving roads and border facilities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geography:** BBIN countries share close geographical proximity, enhancing the need for regional cooperation and connectivity.
 
• **Trade Statistics:** India conducts significant trade with other BBIN countries, making regional transportation vital for economic growth.
 
• **Environmental Concerns:** Bhutan’s hesitation stems from worries about increased vehicular pollution and its impact on the environment.
 
• **Future Prospects:** Successful implementation of the BBIN agreement could pave the way for similar initiatives in other regions, boosting global trade and cooperation.

questions.question: The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation was established in—————.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2001**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)** was officially established on **15 June 2001**, in Shanghai, China.
 
• The founding members of the SCO include **China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan**.
 
• The SCO emerged from the earlier grouping known as the "**Shanghai Five**", which was formed in **1996** to address border security issues between China, Russia, and the Central Asian states.
 
• The organization was established to strengthen relations between member states, promote regional stability, and enhance cooperation on political, economic, security, and cultural matters.
 
• The SCO focuses on combating **terrorism, separatism, and extremism**, along with fostering collaboration in trade, energy, and cultural exchanges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives of SCO:**

 
 
• To strengthen mutual trust and good-neighborly relations among member states.
 
• To promote effective cooperation in **political, economic, trade, scientific, technical, cultural, and environmental spheres**.
 
• To ensure regional peace, security, and stability by addressing **terrorism, drug trafficking, and cross-border crimes**.
 
• To create a fair and rational international political and economic order.
 
 
 
• **Current Member States:**
 
 
• As of now, the SCO has **9 full members**: China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, India, Pakistan, and Iran (added in 2021).
 
• India and Pakistan joined as full members in **2017**.
 
 
 
• **Observer States:**
 
 
• The SCO has several observer states, including **Afghanistan, Belarus, and Mongolia**, which participate in meetings but do not have voting rights.
 
 
 
• **Key Initiatives of SCO:**
 
 
• The SCO promotes projects in **energy, infrastructure, and connectivity** to boost economic cooperation.
 
• It established the **Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS)**, headquartered in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, to combat terrorism and extremism.
 
 
 
• **Importance of SCO:**
 
 
• The SCO covers a significant portion of the Eurasian region, accounting for around **60% of the landmass** and nearly **40% of the global population**.
 
• It serves as a platform for addressing regional issues and building multilateral cooperation among member countries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Evolution of SCO:**

 
 
• Before its establishment in **2001**, the organization functioned as the "**Shanghai Five**", which included China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan.
 
• Uzbekistan joined in **2001**, leading to the creation of the SCO.
 
 
 
• **Significance for India:**
 
 
• India's membership in the SCO provides a platform to enhance **regional cooperation** and address shared challenges like terrorism and extremism.
 
• It allows India to engage with Central Asian countries and strengthen ties with China and Russia.

questions.question: In June 2025, who has been appointed as the Director of Prime Ministers Museum and Library (PMML)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashwani Lohani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ashwani Lohani** has been appointed as the Director of the **Prime Ministers Museum and Library (PMML)** in June 2025. This high-profile appointment reflects his extensive experience in administration and leadership roles.
 
• He is a retired officer of the **Indian Railway Service of Mechanical Engineers (IRSME)** and has previously served as the Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) of **Air India**.
 
• Mr. Lohani is widely recognized for his expertise in managing public sector enterprises and has also headed the **Railway Board**, the apex body of the Indian Railways.
 
• The **Prime Ministers Museum and Library (PMML)**, located in New Delhi, is a premier institution dedicated to preserving and showcasing the contributions of Indian Prime Ministers and their historical significance.
 
• His appointment is expected to enhance the strategic vision and operational efficiency of the PMML, further enriching its role as a repository of India’s political and cultural heritage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Prime Ministers Museum and Library (PMML):**

 
 
• PMML is located in **New Delhi**, India, and is a government-run institution committed to preserving the legacy of Indian Prime Ministers.
 
• It serves as a repository of documents, photographs, and other memorabilia related to the lives and contributions of India’s Prime Ministers.
 
• The museum also houses research facilities and archives that are accessible to scholars and the public.
 
• Its objective is to educate future generations about the socio-political history of India and the visionary leadership of its Prime Ministers.
 
 
 
• **Ashwani Lohani’s Previous Roles:**
 
 
• He has served as the **CMD of Air India**, where he played a critical role in stabilizing the operations of the national carrier during a challenging period.
 
• As the Chairman of the **Railway Board**, he oversaw significant reforms in the Indian Railways, including infrastructure development and safety enhancements.
 
• He is known for his ability to lead large-scale public sector enterprises with a focus on efficiency and innovation.
 
 
 
• **Functions of PMML:**
 
 
• The museum organizes exhibitions, seminars, and workshops to promote awareness about India’s political heritage.
 
• It collaborates with national and international institutions for research and academic exchange programs.
 
• The library within PMML is a resource-rich center for students, historians, and policymakers interested in Indian political history.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of PMML:**

 
 
• The institution is instrumental in documenting the evolution of India’s democracy and the role of its Prime Ministers in shaping the nation.
 
• It provides a platform for citizens to engage with India’s rich political and cultural history.
 
 
 
• **Role of Directors in PMML:**
 
 
• The Director oversees the strategic planning and day-to-day operations of the museum and library.
 
• They are responsible for curating exhibitions, acquiring new collections, and ensuring the institution’s relevance to contemporary audiences.

questions.question: In June 2025, government of India has organized a National Consultation on Gender Budgeting in————— .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vigyan Bhawan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vigyan Bhawan** is an iconic conference center located in **New Delhi, India**, used for hosting national and international events, seminars, and consultations.
 
• The **National Consultation on Gender Budgeting** organized by the Government of India in **June 2025** focused on enhancing strategies to incorporate gender perspectives into budgeting processes.
 
• Gender Budgeting is a **methodology** for analyzing government budgets to ensure equitable resource allocation for women and men, addressing **gender inequalities**.
 
• Vigyan Bhawan has historically been the venue for significant governmental discussions, making it a suitable choice for such consultations.
 
• The consultation witnessed participation from **policy experts, economists, and government officials** to assess the impact of gender-sensitive budgeting practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vigyan Bhawan**:

 
 
• Constructed in **1956**, Vigyan Bhawan serves as a premier venue for government-hosted events, including international conventions and discussions.
 
• It is equipped with state-of-the-art facilities such as conference halls, meeting rooms, and a media center, making it ideal for large-scale consultations.
 
 
 
• **Gender Budgeting**:
 
 
• Gender Budgeting was first introduced by the Government of India in the **2005-2006 Union Budget**.
 
• It aims to integrate a **gender perspective** into financial planning and allocation processes to reduce disparities.
 
• Key features include analyzing resource allocation for women-centric programs and addressing systemic issues affecting **women’s empowerment**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Venues for Government Events:**
 
 
• **Andhra Bhawan:** A residential complex primarily used to accommodate officials and dignitaries from Andhra Pradesh.
 
• **Rail Bhawan:** Headquarters of the Ministry of Railways, primarily used for administrative purposes.
 
• **Hyderabad House:** A heritage building in Delhi, often used for hosting **state dinners** and bilateral meetings.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Gender Budgeting:**
 
 
• Gender Budgeting ensures **inclusive growth** by addressing gender-specific challenges in areas such as **health, education, employment, and social welfare**.
 
• India’s efforts in gender budgeting have inspired other nations to adopt similar approaches to improve gender equity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Government of India Initiatives:**

 
 
• Several ministries incorporate **gender budgeting cells** to ensure targeted resource allocation for addressing women’s issues.
 
• Programs like **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao**, **POSHAN Abhiyaan**, and **STEP (Support to Training and Employment Program for Women)** have been strengthened through gender budgeting.
 
 
 
• **Global Perspective:**
 
 
• Countries like **Australia, South Africa, and the UK** have adopted gender budgeting practices to address gender disparities effectively.
 
• The **UNDP (United Nations Development Programme)** supports nations in implementing gender-sensitive approaches in budgeting.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **Bharatiya Bhasha Pustak Scheme** was introduced in the **Budget 2025** with the aim of promoting Indian languages and literature across diverse regions of India. • The scheme is being implemented under the **Ministry of Education**, which is tasked with fostering cultural and linguistic diversity in the educational ecosystem. • The scheme focuses on creating educational materials and books in regional Indian languages, contributing to the vision of the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**, which emphasizes multilingual education. • The initiative seeks to empower students by providing access to educational resources in their native languages, thereby enhancing inclusivity and learning outcomes. • The **Ministry of Education** plays a pivotal role in coordinating with state governments, educational institutions, and publishers to ensure the successful implementation of this scheme.

questions.question: A Kho-Kho playground (or pitch) is ———— in shape.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**rectangular**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kho-Kho playground** is designed to be **rectangular** in shape, which is the standard and universally accepted dimension for the game.
 
• The dimensions of a Kho-Kho field are typically **29 meters in length** and **16 meters in width** for senior players, as prescribed by the Kho-Kho Federation of India.
 
• It includes a central lane (spanning the length of the field) and **two poles** placed at each end of the field, which are crucial to the gameplay mechanics.
 
• The rectangular shape ensures a clear division of space for the chasers and defenders, facilitating smooth gameplay.
 
• The rectangular field is marked with eight cross lanes, each **16 meters long**, which are perpendicular to the central lane and help in the strategic movement of players.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dimensions and Markings:**

 
 
• The total area of the Kho-Kho field is **29 x 16 meters**, with an additional free zone of **3 meters** at each end of the field.
 
• The two poles at either end of the central lane are placed **2.55 meters** from the end lines.
 
 
 
• **Game Rules and Use of Field:**
 
 
• Khokho is a traditional Indian sport that requires strategic running and agility within the field's boundary.
 
• The game is played between two teams, where one team defends while the other chases, utilizing the rectangular field to tag opponents or evade being tagged.
 
 
 
• **Other Field Shapes in Sports:**
 
 
• **Circular fields** are common in sports like kabaddi or athletics.
 
• **Oval fields** are used in cricket and Australian rules football.
 
• **Square fields** are typically uncommon in sports.
 
 
 
• **Historical and Cultural Significance:**
 
 
• Kho-Kho originated in India and has been played in its rectangular field design since its formalization in the early 20th century.
 
• The sport is now governed internationally by the **Asian Kho-Kho Federation** and the **Kho-Kho Federation of India**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The rectangular design of the Kho-Kho field allows for optimal gameplay by providing clear zones for chasers and defenders.
 
• The central lane and cross lanes are integral to the strategy and movement of players during the game.
 
• Kho-Kho is recognized as one of the **oldest traditional sports** in India and has undergone standardization to ensure uniform gameplay worldwide.
 
• The rectangular field shape has been retained across all levels of play, including school, national, and international competitions.

questions.question: As of 31st July 2025, in which event has India won the greatest number of medals at the Asian Games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Athletics**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Athletics** has been the most successful sport for India at the **Asian Games**. It has brought the country the highest number of medals in the event's history.
 
• The discipline includes a wide variety of events, such as **track and field, marathon, racewalking, and relays**, providing multiple opportunities for medal wins.
 
• India has won numerous **gold, silver, and bronze medals** in athletics over the years. Prominent athletes like **Milkha Singh, P.T. Usha, Neeraj Chopra, and Hima Das** have significantly contributed to India's medal tally.
 
• India's dominance in athletics at the **Asian Games** is attributed to its strong performances in events like **middle-distance running, javelin throw, and long jump**.
 
• As of **31st July 2025**, athletics remains the discipline where India has consistently excelled and secured the highest number of medals compared to other sports like wrestling, shooting, or hockey.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Athletics at the Asian Games:**

 
 
• Athletics has been a part of the **Asian Games** since its inception in **1951**.
 
• The events are categorized into **track events, field events, and road events**.
 
• India has shown consistent performances in **men's and women's track events**, particularly in **relay races** and **hurdles**.
 
 
 
• **Indian Athletics Legends:**
 
 
• **Milkha Singh:** Known as the "Flying Sikh," he won the **gold medal** in the **400m race** at the **1958 Asian Games**.
 
• **P.T. Usha:** She earned the title "Queen of Indian Track and Field" after winning **multiple gold medals** and setting records at the **1986 Asian Games**.
 
• **Neeraj Chopra:** The javelin thrower won **gold** at the **2018 Asian Games**, further solidifying India's legacy in athletics.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Sports:**
 
 
• **Wrestling:** While India has achieved success in wrestling, the number of medals is fewer compared to athletics due to fewer events.
 
• **Shooting:** India has excelled in shooting at recent Asian Games, but it still lags behind athletics in terms of overall medal count.
 
• **Hockey:** India's hockey teams have won multiple gold medals, but the number of events in hockey is limited compared to athletics.
 
 
 
• **Asian Games Performance Data:**
 
 
• India has won over **250 medals** in athletics at the Asian Games, including **85 gold medals** (as of 31st July 2025).
 
• The consistent performance in athletics has been a result of government initiatives, training programs, and the emergence of world-class athletes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Neeraj Chopra's Achievements:** He is the first Indian track and field athlete to win a **gold medal** at the **Olympics**, which has further boosted interest in athletics.
 
• **Infrastructure Development:** India has invested in **state-of-the-art training facilities**, such as the **NIS Patiala**, to nurture future athletes.
 
• **Support Programs:** Initiatives like the **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)** have been instrumental in supporting athletes financially and technically.
 
• **Future Prospects:** With the emergence of young talent and improved training, India is poised to maintain its dominance in athletics at the Asian Games.

questions.question: A long-lost velvet worm species Typhloperipatus Williamsoni, has been rediscovered after 111 years in ———— .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arunachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Typhloperipatus Williamsoni**, a long-lost species of velvet worm, has been rediscovered after **111 years** in the state of **Arunachal Pradesh**, India.
 
• This species belongs to the **Onychophora phylum**, which is often referred to as "living fossils" due to their evolutionary uniqueness and ancient lineage.
 
• The rediscovery of the species highlights the rich **biodiversity** of Arunachal Pradesh, which is part of the **Eastern Himalayas Biodiversity Hotspot**.
 
• Velvet worms are known for their soft, segmented bodies and unique mode of locomotion through slime secretion, which they use to hunt prey.
 
• The rediscovery underscores the importance of **conservation** efforts and biodiversity studies in remote areas like Arunachal Pradesh, which harbor rare and endemic species.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• The **Vettukad Festival**, also known as the **Feast of Christ the King**, is celebrated by the **Christian community** in Kerala.

• It has a historical legacy of over **500 years**, showcasing Portuguese architectural influences.
 
• The church is renowned for its serene ambiance and spiritual significance, attracting visitors throughout the year.

questions.question: The light of the sun takes about ———— minutes to reach the earth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**eight**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The light from the Sun takes approximately **8 minutes and 20 seconds** to travel the distance of about **149.6 million kilometers** (the average distance between the Sun and the Earth).
 
• This time is calculated based on the speed of light, which is approximately **299,792 kilometers per second** in a vacuum.
 
• Light travels at a finite speed, so the sunlight we see is slightly delayed, meaning we observe the Sun as it was about 8 minutes ago.
 
• The phenomenon is crucial for understanding astronomical observations, as light from distant celestial objects takes years, decades, or even centuries to reach Earth.
 
• The **8-minute travel time** is an average, as the distance between the Sun and Earth slightly varies due to the elliptical orbit of Earth around the Sun.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Speed of Light:**

 
 
• The speed of light in a vacuum is a constant and is approximately **299,792 kilometers per second** or **186,282 miles per second**.
 
• This value is a fundamental constant in physics and is denoted by the symbol **c**.
 
• It is the maximum speed at which all energy, matter, and information in the universe can travel.
 
 
 
• **Distance Between Sun and Earth:**
 
 
• The average distance from the Sun to Earth is referred to as an **Astronomical Unit (AU)** and is roughly equal to **149.6 million kilometers**.
 
• The actual distance varies throughout the year due to Earth's elliptical orbit, ranging from **147 million kilometers (perihelion)** to **152 million kilometers (aphelion)**.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Light Travel Time:**
 
 
• Light travel time helps astronomers determine the distance to celestial objects in space.
 
• For instance, the light from the Moon takes about **1.3 seconds** to reach Earth, while light from the closest star (other than the Sun), Proxima Centauri, takes about **4.24 years**.
 
 
 
• **Application in Astronomy:**
 
 
• The concept of light travel time allows scientists to observe the past states of celestial bodies, as we are essentially seeing them as they were when the light left them.
 
• This delay helps in studying the history and evolution of stars, galaxies, and the universe itself.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Light Year:** A light year is the distance that light travels in one year, approximately **9.46 trillion kilometers**. It is a unit often used to measure astronomical distances.
 
• **Solar Constant:** The energy received per unit area from the Sun at the top of Earth's atmosphere is known as the solar constant, approximately **1361 watts per square meter**.
 
• **Relativity of Time:** The finite speed of light is a cornerstone of Einstein's theory of relativity, implying that time and space are interlinked and relative to the observer's frame of reference.
 
• **Implications for Space Exploration:** Light travel time affects communication with spacecraft. For instance, signals from Mars take about **13 minutes** to reach Earth when the planets are at their farthest distance from each other.

questions.question: Which unconventional clean energy source in Earth's crust, seen as a potential jackpot for 170000 years of power, gained attention in May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Natural hydrogen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Natural hydrogen** refers to hydrogen gas naturally produced in the Earth's crust, often found as a result of geological processes such as water-rock interaction, radiolysis, or serpentinization of ultramafic rocks.
 
• In **May 2025**, attention surged on natural hydrogen as a potential energy source due to its abundance and sustainability. It is often termed as "white hydrogen" in contrast to industrially-produced hydrogen (green, blue, or grey hydrogen).
 
• Studies have indicated that **natural hydrogen reservoirs** could potentially supply energy for up to **170,000 years**, making it a game-changer in renewable energy.
 
• Unlike other hydrogen production methods, natural hydrogen extraction has a low-carbon footprint, as it does not require energy-intensive processes like electrolysis or steam methane reforming.
 
• Countries like **Australia**, **Brazil**, and **Mali** have already started exploring natural hydrogen deposits, recognizing their potential to reduce reliance on fossil fuels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Natural Hydrogen Characteristics:**

 
 
• Often referred to as **geological hydrogen** or **white hydrogen**, it is formed naturally in the Earth's crust and mantle.
 
• It is associated with processes like **serpentinization**, where water reacts with certain rock types (e.g., peridotite) to release hydrogen gas.
 
• Natural hydrogen can seep to the Earth's surface through fractures and faults, creating **hydrogen seeps**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Hydrogen Types:**
 
 
• **Green hydrogen:** Produced through electrolysis powered by renewable energy.
 
• **Blue hydrogen:** Derived from natural gas with carbon capture and storage to reduce emissions.
 
• **Grey hydrogen:** Generated from fossil fuels without carbon capture, leading to high emissions.
 
 
 
• **Global Exploration:**
 
 
• In **Mali**, a natural hydrogen well discovered in 1987 has been operational and producing clean hydrogen for local use.
 
• **Australia** and **Brazil** have conducted surveys and identified promising sites for natural hydrogen extraction.
 
• Research is underway to map global hydrogen seeps and understand the geological conditions necessary for their formation.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Natural Hydrogen:**
 
 
• It is a **renewable and low-emission energy source** with minimal environmental impact during extraction.
 
• Offers a cost-effective alternative to industrially-produced hydrogen due to the absence of energy-intensive production processes.
 
• Its abundance in Earth's crust could provide a stable and long-term energy supply.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geological Context:**

 
 
• Natural hydrogen is often found in **cratonic regions** (ancient, stable parts of the Earth's crust).
 
• Seeps are more common in areas with **fractured rocks** and **tectonic activity**.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• Extraction of natural hydrogen has a **lower carbon footprint** compared to conventional fossil fuels.
 
• Does not require significant water resources, unlike green hydrogen production via electrolysis.
 
 
 
• **Economic Potential:**
 
 
• Natural hydrogen has the potential to be a cost-effective energy source, reducing dependency on fossil fuels.
 
• Investments in exploration and extraction technologies are increasing globally, aiming to harness this resource efficiently.

questions.question: In which year Indian Arms Act was passed by British Government?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1878**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Arms Act** was passed by the **British Government in 1878** during the tenure of Viceroy Lord Lytton.
 
• The Act was introduced to **disarm the Indian population** and maintain British control over the region, especially after the Revolt of 1857.
 
• It mandated that Indians needed a **license to own, carry, or sell arms and ammunition**, while Europeans in India were largely exempt from this restriction.
 
• The Act was a key measure to **suppress potential uprisings** and ensure British dominance by limiting access to weapons.
 
• The discrimination embedded in the Act became a symbol of colonial oppression and was later criticized by Indian leaders, including **Mahatma Gandhi**, during the freedom struggle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Background of the Indian Arms Act (1878):**

 
 
• The Act was passed in the aftermath of the **First War of Independence (1857)**, also known as the Sepoy Mutiny, where Indians used arms against British forces.
 
• The British Government feared another rebellion and sought to limit the Indian population's ability to access weapons.
 
 
 
• **Provisions of the Act:**
 
 
• The Act required Indians to obtain a **license** for possessing firearms.
 
• It imposed **harsh penalties** for those caught possessing arms without proper authorization.
 
• Europeans in India were **exempted** from these restrictions, highlighting the racial discrimination of colonial policies.
 
 
 
• **Criticism of the Act:**
 
 
• Indian leaders and freedom fighters viewed the Act as a tool of **oppression** and a means to suppress dissent.
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi** referred to the Indian Arms Act as one of the most humiliating pieces of legislation enacted by the British.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Act:**
 
 
• The Act restricted the ability of Indians to defend themselves or organize armed resistance against the British Empire.
 
• It remained in force until India gained independence in **1947** and was later replaced by new legislation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Act was part of a broader British strategy to maintain control over India by weakening its military and organizational capabilities.
 
• The discriminatory nature of the Act also played a role in fueling nationalist sentiments and demands for equality and self-rule.
 
• After independence, the Indian Government replaced colonial-era laws with the **Arms Act of 1959**, which aimed to regulate arms while respecting citizens' rights.

questions.question: Who among the following holds office during the pleasure of the President of India?

options.text: Comptroller and Auditor General of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Attorney General of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Attorney General of India** is the chief legal advisor to the Government of India and is appointed by the **President of India** under **Article 76** of the Constitution.
 
• The Attorney General holds office **during the pleasure of the President**. This means the tenure is not fixed and depends solely on the President's discretion.
 
• The Attorney General has the right to participate in the proceedings of both Houses of Parliament but **does not have voting rights**.
 
• The Attorney General is responsible for advising the government on legal matters and performing other legal duties assigned by the President.
 
• Unlike other constitutional functionaries, such as the **Chief Justice of India** or **Comptroller and Auditor General**, the Attorney General does not enjoy security of tenure, as they serve at the President's pleasure.
 
• **Hence, the Attorney General of India holds office during the pleasure of the President of India.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG):**

 
 
• Appointed under **Article 148** of the Indian Constitution, the CAG is responsible for auditing accounts of the government and public sector organizations.
 
• The CAG enjoys security of tenure and cannot be removed from office except through a process similar to the impeachment of a Supreme Court judge.
 
• The CAG does not hold office during the pleasure of the President.
 
 
 
• **Chief Justice of India (CJI):**
 
 
• The CJI is appointed by the President under **Article 124** of the Constitution and is the head of the judiciary system in India.
 
• The CJI serves until the age of **65 years** and cannot be arbitrarily removed by the President, ensuring independence.
 
• The Chief Justice does not hold office during the pleasure of the President.
 
 
 
• **Chief Election Commissioner (CEC):**
 
 
• Appointed under **Article 324** of the Constitution, the CEC oversees free and fair elections in India.
 
• The CEC enjoys security of tenure and can only be removed in the manner prescribed for Supreme Court judges.
 
• The Chief Election Commissioner does not hold office during the pleasure of the President.
 
 
 
• **Function of the Attorney General:**
 
 
• The Attorney General represents the Government of India in legal cases before the Supreme Court and High Courts.
 
• They can take part in parliamentary debates and discussions and advise the government on constitutional and legal matters.
 
• The Attorney General is not considered a government servant and can engage in private practice, provided it does not conflict with their duties.
 
• The position of Attorney General is modeled after the British system, where the Attorney General serves as the chief legal adviser to the Crown.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tenure and Removal:**

 
 
• The Attorney General does not have a fixed tenure and can be removed or replaced at any time by the President.
 
• This flexible arrangement ensures that the Attorney General remains aligned with the government's priorities and policies.
 
 
 
• **Legal Framework:**
 
 
• Articles **74, 76, and 88** of the Constitution define the role and powers of the Attorney General.
 
• The Attorney General's primary responsibility is to maintain the government's legal integrity and represent it in judicial matters.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility Criteria:**
 
 
• The Attorney General must be qualified to be appointed as a judge of the Supreme Court, requiring a minimum of **five years of experience as a High Court judge** or **10 years of legal practice**.
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• Prominent Attorney Generals of India include **M.C. Setalvad** (the first Attorney General), **Soli Sorabjee**, and **K.K. Venugopal**.

questions.question: The period from ———— is referred to as a period of stagnant or stationary phase of growth of India's population.
questions.solution: The correct answer is __**1901-1921**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • The period **1901-1921** is referred to as the **stagnant or stationary phase** of India's population growth. • During this phase, the **population growth rate was almost negligible** due to high birth and death rates balancing each other. • India experienced frequent **famines, epidemics, and pandemics** like the influenza pandemic of 1918-19, which caused significant loss of life. • The absence of modern healthcare, sanitation, and public health measures further contributed to the **high mortality rate** during this time. • This phase is marked by a **low and fluctuating population growth rate**, which is why it is termed as the stagnant phase.

questions.question: If the government continues to borrow year after year, it leads to the ———.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**accumulation of debt**__.

• If the government continues to borrow year after year, it leads to the **accumulation of debt**. This is due to the fact that borrowed funds need to be repaid, often with interest, thereby increasing the financial liabilities over time.

• **Debt traps** can occur when the government borrows to repay previous loans, leading to a vicious cycle of borrowing and repayment without addressing the underlying fiscal issues.

questions.question: Do Which of the following endocrine gland releases hormone related to puberty in human females?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ovaries**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **ovaries** are a pair of female reproductive glands located on either side of the uterus in the pelvic cavity. They are part of the endocrine system and play a key role in regulating puberty.
 
• Ovaries produce and release **sex hormones** such as **estrogen** and **progesterone**, which are crucial for the development of secondary sexual characteristics during puberty.
 
• **Estrogen** is the primary hormone responsible for the development of female characteristics such as breast development, widening of hips, and the regulation of the menstrual cycle.
 
• During puberty, the ovaries also begin releasing **mature eggs** (ova) through the process of ovulation, which is essential for reproduction.
 
• These hormonal changes are initiated under the influence of the **hypothalamus** and **pituitary gland**, which release gonadotropins such as luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) to stimulate ovarian activity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pancreas:**

 
 
• The pancreas is a mixed gland that functions as both an endocrine and exocrine gland.
 
• The endocrine part of the pancreas secretes **insulin** and **glucagon**, which regulate blood sugar levels, but it does not play a direct role in puberty.
 
 
 
• **Pineal Gland:**
 
 
• The pineal gland is a small endocrine gland located in the brain and is responsible for the production of the hormone **melatonin**.
 
• Melatonin regulates sleep-wake cycles but does not influence puberty in females.
 
 
 
• **Hypothalamus:**
 
 
• The hypothalamus is a part of the brain that regulates various hormonal processes by releasing **gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH)**.
 
• GnRH stimulates the pituitary gland to release LH and FSH, which in turn stimulate the ovaries. While essential, the hypothalamus itself does not release puberty-specific hormones directly.
 
 
 
• **Ovaries:**
 
 
• The ovaries are the primary endocrine glands responsible for the hormonal changes associated with puberty in human females.
 
• They produce **estrogen**, which triggers the development of secondary sexual characteristics and prepares the body for reproduction.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Estrogen:**

 
 
• Estrogen is essential for the development of primary and secondary sexual characteristics such as breast enlargement, fat distribution in hips and thighs, and the growth of the endometrial lining in the uterus.
 
• This hormone also regulates the menstrual cycle and supports reproductive health.
 
 
 
• **Age of Puberty:**
 
 
• Puberty in females generally begins between the ages of **8 and 13**, with significant hormonal changes occurring during this time.
 
 
 
• **Menstrual Cycle:**
 
 
• The ovaries play a critical role in the menstrual cycle by releasing eggs and producing hormones like estrogen and progesterone that regulate the cycle.
